_comment: The bean graph for the `qou` instance. Mirrors the platform's own `beans/beans.json` (litlfred/folio-assistant, `beans/` layout): the DIRECTORIES of the graph are declared here, paths resolve against this file's directory, so the whole graph relocates by moving one folder. Added 2026-09-26 with the `.beans/` -> `beans/defs/` move (bean qou-utbr), on the owner's 2026-09-26 instruction to align to folio-assistant unless there is a specific reason not to.
_beans_yml_comment: `.beans.yml` at the repo root STILL carries `path: beans/defs` and must keep agreeing with the `defs` entry below. That duplication is deliberate and is the platform's own note, verbatim: 'NOTE: `.beans.yml` still carries the defs path because the `beans` binary is third-party; `bun run check:harness-dirs` fails when they disagree.' The `beans` CLI is hmans/beans and reads only `.beans.yml`; it knows nothing about this file.
name: qou

directories.description: Work items — one Markdown file each, in the layout the `beans` CLI reads. Also holds the watcher queue JSON files (`*-queue.json`) that AGENTS.md work-plan §4 names.

_no_archive_comment: NO `defs/archive/` IS CREATED HERE, deliberately. The platform has one (631 of its 1,003 beans), and the tempting reading is that it removes completed beans from the working set. MEASURED, IT DOES NOT: the `beans` CLI RECURSES into a subdirectory of the defs path, so an archived bean still appears in `beans list`. Controlled fixture, 2026-09-26: a scratch tree with one bean in `defs/` and one in `defs/archive/` returns BOTH. So an archive buys git/grep/editor tidiness and nothing for `beans list`, the §4 idle-backlog policy, or the session-start sweep. Whether qou wants it on those grounds alone is an open question, not a scale fix — see bean qou-utbr, which carries the retraction of the scale claim.
_no_workflows_comment: The platform also declares a `workflows` directory (running BPMN instances, `folio-workflow-instance/v1`). qou has none, so it is not declared — an empty declared directory would assert a graph part that does not exist.
